ground_truth_soap:
Subjective:

Chief Complaint (CC):
Obesity and associated symptoms.

History of Present Illness (HPI):
The patient, Mr. Hiroshi Tanaka, is a 62-year-old Asian male presenting with concerns related to obesity, which has been persistent for the past 2 years. He reports moderate severity, with daily occurrences of symptoms including persistent fatigue and lower extremity edema. These symptoms have significantly affected his ability to perform physical activities such as climbing stairs and carrying groceries, though he can manage desk job tasks.

The patient has a history of hypothyroidism, managed with levothyroxine 75 mcg daily. He follows an irregular diet high in starchy foods and engages in infrequent exercise, primarily occasional walking. He sleeps 8 hours per night but feels unrefreshed upon waking. He does not use tobacco, consumes alcohol socially 1-2 times per month, and denies any drug use. He enjoys gardening but is limited by his physical capacity.

Review of Systems (ROS):
- Constitutional: Reports fatigue.
- Respiratory: Denies shortness of breath or cough.
- Cardiovascular: Reports mild bilateral pedal edema.
- Gastrointestinal: Denies changes in bowel habits, no history of nausea or vomiting.
- Musculoskeletal: Reports difficulty with physical activities such as climbing stairs.
- Endocrine: Managed hypothyroidism, no new symptoms reported.

Objective:

Vital Signs:
- Blood Pressure: 128/78 mmHg
- BMI: 34.5 kg/m²

General Appearance:
- No acute distress, overweight, alert.

Extremities:
- Mild bilateral pedal edema observed.

Assessment:
- Obesity, unspecified.
- Persistent fatigue and lower extremity edema likely secondary to obesity.

Plan:
Lifestyle Modification:
   - Prescribed a Mediterranean diet plan.
   - Encouraged joining a community gym membership for regular exercise.
   
Follow-Up:
   - Bi-weekly virtual follow-up with a dietitian for the next 3 months to monitor dietary changes and weight management.

Referrals:
   - Referred to physical therapy for a tailored weight-bearing exercise program. Reason: To improve physical capacity and manage obesity. Specialist: Physical Therapist. Doctor: Dr. Emily Johnson.

Medications:
   - No new medications prescribed; continue with levothyroxine 75 mcg daily.

Investigations:
   - Ordered a biochemistry panel including fasting lipid profile, fasting blood glucose, and HbA1c to assess metabolic status.

The patient is highly cooperative and motivated to make lifestyle changes. He resides in an urban, affluent neighborhood with good access to parks and recreational facilities, and minimal environmental health risks. Given his high health literacy and fluency in English, patient education materials regarding the Mediterranean diet and exercise regimens were provided. Follow-up results of the biochemistry panel are pending and will be reviewed in subsequent consultations.
